claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Combining a GNN trained on hierarchical heterostructure descriptors with CALPHAD-derived data will improve prediction accuracy for Young’s modulus.
Combining a GNN trained on hierarchical heterostructure descriptors with CALPHAD-derived data will improve prediction accuracy for yield strength.
Combining a GNN trained on hierarchical heterostructure descriptors with CALPHAD-derived data will improve prediction accuracy for toughness.
The hybrid GNN-CALPHAD approach will improve computational efficiency.
Local chemical-environment, phase-distribution, and defect-density descriptors can represent the relevant hierarchical heterostructure.
Hierarchical heterostructure descriptors capture multilevel chemical fluctuations and phase interactions.
A GNN can use the proposed descriptors to capture complex local interactions within HfNbTiVAl10.
A GNN can use the proposed descriptors to capture complex global interactions within HfNbTiVAl10.
CALPHAD-derived thermodynamic parameters provide a physics-informed baseline for phase stability.
CALPHAD-derived thermodynamic parameters provide a physics-informed baseline for composition-property relationships.
The hybrid approach reduces reliance on computationally expensive first-principles calculations.
Incorporating multiscale structural information improves mechanical-property prediction accuracy.
The model will deliver at least a 20% accuracy improvement for Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
The model will deliver at least a 30% improvement in computational efficiency.
The proposed model may become unreliable for alloys with significantly different hierarchical heterostructures.
The proposed model may become unreliable for properties governed by phenomena absent from its descriptors, such as high-temperature creep.
The magnitude of the accuracy and efficiency gains depends on the quality and representativeness of the GNN training data.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome defines the comparator as prior models trained solely on thermophysical parameters, whereas the baseline defines it as models trained on thermophysical parameters and CALPHAD data.
